note.explanation: Cellular respiration releases energy by oxidizing food inside cells. With oxygen, glucose is completely oxidized and releases more energy; without oxygen, glucose is incompletely oxidized and releases less energy. The main stages of aerobic respiration are glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain.
examples: In yeast, pyruvic acid is converted into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide.
In hard-working muscles when oxygen is insufficient, pyruvic acid is converted into lactic acid.
note.checkAnswer: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen.
note.simple: Cells release energy from food. Oxygen allows more energy to be released; without enough oxygen, cells release less.
note.checkQuestion: Where does glycolysis occur, and does it need oxygen?
note.title: Cellular Respiration
steps: In glycolysis, one glucose molecule is broken into two pyruvic acid molecules in the cytoplasm.
When oxygen is available, pyruvic acid is converted into acetyl coenzyme-A and enters the Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix.
The Krebs cycle produces carbon dioxide, ATP, NADH and FADH₂.
In the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membranes, electrons release energy used to make ATP; oxygen combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.
note.answer: Cellular respiration is the oxidation of food inside cells to release energy.

rationales: Correct: glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
Incorrect: the mitochondrial matrix is where the Krebs cycle occurs.
Incorrect: the inner mitochondrial membrane is where the electron transport chain occurs.
Incorrect: glycolysis does not occur in the nucleus.

options: It produces lactic acid in every cell.

written.text: Explain the types and importance of anaerobic respiration.
written.finalAnswer: Anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen and incompletely oxidizes glucose, releasing less energy. Alcoholic fermentation occurs in yeast and some bacteria: pyruvic acid is converted into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide. Lactic acid fermentation occurs in skeletal muscles of humans and other animals: pyruvic acid is converted into lactic acid. Anaerobic respiration provided energy to early organisms, is used by anaerobes and by muscles when oxygen is insufficient, and fermentation is used to make products such as cheese, yogurt, alcohol, bread and soy sauce.

written.text: Outline the mechanism of aerobic respiration.
written.finalAnswer: Aerobic respiration has three main steps: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, where glucose is broken into two pyruvic acid molecules, producing two ATP and two NADH. In the mitochondrial matrix, pyruvic acid is converted into acetyl coenzyme-A, then completely oxidized in the Krebs cycle to carbon dioxide, ATP, NADH and FADH₂. On the inner mitochondrial membranes, NADH and FADH₂ release electrons and hydrogen ions; electron flow releases energy used to make ATP, and oxygen combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.

written.finalAnswer: Photosynthesis is an anabolic process that stores energy in bond energy, occurs in chloroplasts in green parts, is performed by some bacteria, all algae and all plants, and occurs in daytime in the presence of light. Respiration is a catabolic process that transforms the bond energy of food into ATP, occurs in the cytoplasm and mitochondria of all cells, is performed by all organisms, and occurs all the time.

written.text: How does the structure of ATP enable it to store and release energy efficiently?
written.finalAnswer: ATP stores energy in its phosphate bonds. When its terminal phosphate bond is broken, ATP becomes ADP and a phosphate group, releasing energy for cellular activities. Energy from respiration can be used to add a phosphate group to ADP to reform ATP.

examTips: Short questions may ask for the definitions of aerobic and anaerobic respiration, products of fermentation, or the purpose of cellular respiration.
For a 2-mark definition or explanation, include the key condition or product as well as the main idea; for example, anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen.
Long questions often ask for the types and importance of anaerobic respiration or the stages of aerobic respiration. Organize answers with clear headings and keep the order of stages correct.
For the aerobic mechanism, marks are earned by naming each stage, giving its location, stating its main change or products, and explaining oxygen's role at the end of the electron transport chain.
For comparison questions, set out matching characteristics for both processes, such as type, energy change, site, organisms and time of occurrence.

explain.title: Cellular respiration releases energy
explain.body: Organisms get energy by breaking the C-H bonds of food. For this purpose, they carry out the oxidation of food inside cells. This oxidation of food is called cellular respiration. The most common food used by cells to get energy is glucose.

explain.title: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen
explain.body: Cellular respiration occurring in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration. It is the complete oxidation of glucose with maximum release of energy.

explain.title: Anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen
explain.body: Cellular respiration that occurs in the absence of oxygen is called anaerobic respiration. In anaerobic respiration, glucose is incompletely oxidized with less amount of energy released.

explain.title: Fermentation has two forms
explain.body: During alcoholic fermentation, pyruvic acid is further broken down into alcohol and CO₂. During lactic acid fermentation in skeletal muscles, pyruvic acid is converted into lactic acid.

explain.title: Aerobic respiration has three main steps
explain.body: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm. The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix. The electron transport chain occurs on the inner membranes of mitochondria and uses released energy to make ATP.

mistakes: Do not confuse aerobic respiration, which occurs in the presence of oxygen, with anaerobic respiration, which occurs in its absence.
Do not say that glycolysis requires oxygen; the section states that oxygen is not required.
Do not mix up fermentation products: yeast forms ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide, while skeletal muscles form lactic acid.
Do not put the Krebs cycle in the cytoplasm; it occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
Do not put the electron transport chain in the mitochondrial matrix; it occurs on the inner mitochondrial membranes.
When explaining the electron transport chain, do not omit that oxygen combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.
